criteria.commensurate: Measured cost about zero against a lint-driven, behavior-preserving refactor. The stages the report says grew (homesteads +1.0, windbreak +0.5, hinterland +0.2 s) are flat or lower at the end commit under equal conditions: medians homesteads 3.66 to 3.56, windbreak 1.42 to 1.36, hinterland 1.28 to 1.25 s. The bookend +14.2% (13.4 to 15.3 s) is inferred to be load. Both bookends sit off this machine history: the 328 series had TOTAL 16.5-17.5 s and 40/39 at 10.4-12.4 s, while 370-start had TOTAL 25.6 s (40/4 25.8 vs about 17) and 370-end had 40/4 20.7, 40/25 16.5 and 40/47 17.4 vs about 17.3/13.5/13.0. The -32% TOTAL and -9.1% at 40 households are the same artifact in reverse, not a speedup.
criteria.necessary: The flagged cost does not exist when measured. The work is necessary in its own right: spec 370 FR-001/FR-002 cap functions at 100 statements, so the 12 over-cap functions had to be split, with the pool byte-identical. The 40-household seed 39 roll does identical work at both commits (placer_calls 158 and 158, houses 40 and 40). Reviewer counterfactual: detached worktrees at a1e5f51a0 (370-start) and e9a10bfb2 (370-end), seed 39 at 40 households, 6 interleaved ABBA pairs, per-stage process CPU time. Median CPU start 12.74 s vs end 12.51 s; paired end/start median 0.986 (all six 0.92-1.00); wall medians 10.99 vs 10.66 s.
criteria.no_way_around: None needed, since there is no cost to avoid. The split adds call boundaries but no per-candidate scans, and placer_calls are unchanged; CPU time shows the added calls are not measurable at this resolution (end/start 0.986). No profile was taken because there is no growth to locate. Caveat: the bookends record no load figure, and their load is inferred from the whole-run totals above. Load average was about 10 on 22 cpus when this audit began and 2-6 during its runs, so a re-taken 370-end on a quiet machine would bring the recorded band back in line.
